sections.heading: Understanding MT940 Tag Structure in Detail
paragraphs: The :20 tag carries the statement reference number, a unique identifier the bank assigns to this particular statement. When reconciling multiple months, this reference helps you match each spreadsheet back to the original statement period and source file.

Balance tags :60M and :62M bracket every statement with opening and closing balances. Each balance line includes a credit-or-debit indicator, a date in YYMMDD format, a currency code and the amount. These bookend figures let reconciliation software verify that no transactions were lost between periods.

Transaction lines in :61 carry a compact structure: date, value date, credit-or-debit marker, amount, transaction type and reference codes. The :86 tag that follows each :61 provides the human-readable narrative, which is where bank charges, wire references and invoice numbers typically appear.

sections.heading: Handling Multiple Statements and Account Types
paragraphs: A single MT940 file can contain statements for several accounts or multiple periods for one account. The converter separates each statement block so you get distinct sheets or clearly labeled sections, preventing data from different accounts from merging into a single ambiguous table.

Account identifiers in the :25 tag distinguish between current accounts, savings accounts and foreign currency holdings. Keeping these labels in the spreadsheet means finance teams can filter by account type without manually sorting through a combined list.

Statement reference sequences help identify chronological order when multiple files arrive across a fiscal year. Preserving these references in the spreadsheet gives auditors a reliable trail from the earliest to the latest statement without guesswork.

sections.heading: From Spreadsheet to Accounting Software
paragraphs: Once the MT940 data sits in Excel, import it into accounting platforms through their CSV or Excel upload features. Most popular tools accept tabular data with standard column headers, so the parsed spreadsheet plugs directly into bookkeeping workflows.

Pivot tables summarize spending by category, date range or counterparty within seconds. Accountants gain instant visibility into cash flow patterns that would take hours to assemble from raw MT940 text.

Conditional formatting highlights unusually large transactions, duplicate entries or dates that fall outside expected ranges. These visual flags surface anomalies early, before they propagate through monthly close processes.
